title: Don Byas in New York and later years

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: sit down there and liable to cause something else, and in this place nobody knows Don Bias, and they care less who Don Bias is really. And he's got his money out, about $800, $900 on him, in one of these big long pocketbooks and had it flashing out his back pocket." I said, "Don, things aren't like they used to be. When you was up here 24 years ago they'd kill you for that amount of money. Now they'll kill you with people looking for that amount of money nowadays." So I had to get a cab and send him home and I got this cab and he didn't know where he lived, but luckily I got a good cab driver, a very nice man. He says, everybody know where he lives. I said Don, "if this cab driver takes you where you think you live, would you know the vicinity of just where you live?" He says yeah, but he did get home all right, because he called me the next day. And then after he finished that concert tour and the record dates in Chicago, he went to New York. Well all the guys in New York knew Don and they knew that he was back with his dues, union dues, after being out of New York for 24 years, but the union squared it up and got him so they give him a tentative card until he finished the concerts and things. So a bunch of musicians got together and met him out to the airport. Just was beautiful you know, he was happy to see everybody. Well Don was in New York around about two or three days. After He

did a couple more concerts and got a few more dollars in his pocket, then's when he started getting wild, drinking again and thinking that Harlem was the same place that he left 24 years ago and it wasn't, until somebody called Eddie Barefield and says, 'oh man, come up here and get your man. He's up here at Basie's place, which was 132nd and 7th Avenue and he's up here going wild, flashing his money and all that.' So I guess Eddie and them went up there and got him and took him home and I didn't hear no more about him. He didn't stay around, I know they cut his tour down quite a bit because they didn't want to be bothered with Don, he was getting out of hand a little bit.
Well I guess Art Blakey had him tour with his group for a little while.

Because I guess from what I've read, Don really wasn't getting much work. So .Blakey said come on with me and I guess they went to Japan, I heard.
And then he went back to Europe and he died not long afterwards.
Was he drinking an awful lot then? I don't know.

I heard, yah. I heard Dan Morganstern said Byas told him that he didn't want to come back for the longest time because he was afraid he'd run into his old buddies and start drinking again. And I guess that's exactly what happened. He wasn't drinking, you know, or at least as much when he was in Europe.
That's too bad. That's too bad. Great tenor player.
